1	package cmd
     2	
     3	import (
     4		"fmt"
     5		"os"
     6		"strings"
     7	
     8		"github.com/mvwi/wt/internal/git"
     9		"github.com/mvwi/wt/internal/github"
    10		"github.com/mvwi/wt/internal/tui"
    11		"github.com/mvwi/wt/internal/ui"
    12		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
    13	)
    14	
    15	var dashCmd = &cobra.Command{
    16		Use:     "dash",
    17		Aliases: []string{"dashboard"},
    18		GroupID: groupWorkflow,
    19		Short:   "Live worktree dashboard (TUI)",
    20		Long: `Interactive worktree dashboard.
    21	
    22	Renders the same data as 'wt list' but refreshes periodically and supports
    23	keyboard navigation. Press enter on a row to switch to that worktree.
    24	
    25	For one-shot or scripted output, use 'wt list' instead.`,
    26		Example: `  wt dash   Open the live dashboard`,
    27		RunE:    runDash,
    28	}
    29	
    30	func init() {
    31		rootCmd.AddCommand(dashCmd)
    32	}
    33	
    34	func runDash(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
    35		if !ui.IsTTY() {
    36			return fmt.Errorf("wt dash requires a terminal\n   For scripted output, use: wt list --output json")
    37		}
    38	
    39		ctx, err := newContext()
    40		if err != nil {
    41			return err
    42		}
    43	
    44		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
    45		if err != nil {
    46			return fmt.Errorf("cannot determine current directory: %w", err)
    47		}
    48	
    49		// Initial load — show a spinner while we collect the slow PR data so the
    50		// TUI starts up with a fully populated table.
    51		spin := ui.NewSpinner("Loading dashboard")
    52		initial, err := gatherDashItems(ctx, cwd)
    53		spin.Stop()
    54		if err != nil {
    55			return err
    56		}
    57	
    58		gather := func() ([]tui.DashItem, error) {
    59			// On each tick, re-read cwd in case the user switched in another shell.
    60			// We don't update the closure's cwd value because IsCurrent is a UX hint,
    61			// not a correctness requirement.
    62			return gatherDashItems(ctx, cwd)
    63		}
    64	
    65		closeFn := func(path, branch string) error {
    66			// RemoveWorktree passes --force, so dirty/unpushed worktrees are
    67			// removable from here. The dashboard already gates risky closes behind
    68			// a confirmation prompt — by the time we get here, the user agreed.
    69			if err := git.RemoveWorktree(path); err != nil {
    70				return err
    71			}
    72			if branch != "" && git.BranchExists(branch) {
    73				_ = git.DeleteBranch(branch)
    74			}
    75			return nil
    76		}
    77	
    78		fetchDetail := func(item tui.DashItem) (tui.DashDetail, error) {
    79			return gatherDashDetail(ctx, item)
    80		}
    81	
    82		rebase := func(path, branch string) (int, error) {
    83			return dashRebase(ctx, path, branch)
    84		}
    85	
    86		result, err := tui.RunDashboard(tui.DashConfig{
    87			Initial:           initial,
    88			Gather:            gather,
    89			Close:             closeFn,
    90			FetchDetail:       fetchDetail,
    91			FetchCommitDetail: gatherCommitDetail,
    92			Rebase:            rebase,
    93		})
    94		if err != nil {
    95			return err
    96		}
    97	
    98		if result.SwitchTo != "" && result.SwitchTo != cwd {
    99			savePreviousWorktree(cwd)
   100			ui.PrintCdHint(result.SwitchTo)
   101			short := ctx.shortName(result.SwitchTo)
   102			fmt.Printf("%s %s\n", ui.Yellow(ui.Current), short)
   103		}
   104	
   105		return nil
   106	}
   107	
   108	// gatherDashDetail produces the bottom-panel detail for one worktree.
   109	// Skips PR lookup when the row has no associated PR. All errors from
   110	// individual git/gh calls are tolerated — the partial result is still useful.
   111	func gatherDashDetail(ctx *cmdContext, item tui.DashItem) (tui.DashDetail, error) {
   112		var d tui.DashDetail
   113	
   114		if item.IsBase {
   115			return d, nil
   116		}
   117	
   118		base := ctx.baseRef()
   119	
   120		// Recent commits (best-effort)
   121		if entries, err := git.LogOnelineIn(item.Path, base, 5); err == nil {
   122			for _, e := range entries {
   123				d.Commits = append(d.Commits, tui.DashCommit{
   124					Hash:    e.Hash,
   125					Subject: e.Subject,
   126					Age:     e.Age,
   127				})
   128			}
   129		}
   130	
   131		// Diff stats (best-effort)
   132		if stats, err := git.DiffStatsIn(item.Path, base); err == nil {
   133			d.Stats = tui.DashDiffStats{
   134				Commits:   stats.Commits,
   135				Files:     stats.Files,
   136				Additions: stats.Additions,
   137				Deletions: stats.Deletions,
   138			}
   139		}
   140	
   141		// File-by-file changes (best-effort)
   142		if files, err := git.DiffFilesIn(item.Path, base); err == nil {
   143			for _, f := range files {
   144				d.Files = append(d.Files, tui.DashFileChange{Status: f.Status, Path: f.Path})
   145			}
   146		}
   147	
   148		// PR detail — title/author/body + named CI checks come from one gh call.
   149		if item.PR != nil && github.IsAvailable() {
   150			if pr, err := github.GetPRDetail(item.PR.Number); err == nil && pr != nil {
   151				d.PRTitle = pr.Title
   152				d.PRAuthor = pr.Author.Login
   153				d.PRBody = firstParagraph(pr.Body)
   154				if item.PR.State == "open" {
   155					for _, c := range pr.StatusChecks {
   156						if c.Name == "" {
   157							continue
   158						}
   159						d.Checks = append(d.Checks, tui.DashCheck{Name: c.Name, State: c.Result()})
   160					}
   161				}
   162			}
   163		}
   164	
   165		return d, nil
   166	}
   167	
   168	// dashRebase syncs a worktree with its upstream. For feature branches that
   169	// means rebasing onto the configured base branch; for the base-branch worktree
   170	// itself it means fast-forwarding from the remote (since rebasing the base
   171	// onto itself is meaningless). Async-safe for use from the dashboard's
   172	// tea.Cmd: never prompts, never auto-stashes, aborts cleanly on conflict.
   173	// Returns the number of commits applied and an error describing why the
   174	// operation didn't proceed (dirty, conflicts, etc.).
   175	func dashRebase(ctx *cmdContext, path, branch string) (int, error) {
   176		if git.HasChangesIn(path) {
   177			return 0, fmt.Errorf("uncommitted changes")
   178		}
   179	
   180		if ctx.isBaseBranch(branch) {
   181			return dashFastForwardBase(ctx, path)
   182		}
   183	
   184		// Fetch the base ref so the rebase target is current. Failure here is
   185		// non-fatal — fall through to rebase against whatever's local.
   186		_ = git.Fetch(ctx.Config.Remote, ctx.Config.BaseBranch)
   187	
   188		ab, err := git.GetAheadBehindIn(path, ctx.baseRef())
   189		if err != nil {
   190			return 0, err
   191		}
   192		if ab.Behind == 0 {
   193			return 0, nil // up to date
   194		}
   195		if err := git.RebaseIn(path, ctx.baseRef()); err != nil {
   196			git.RebaseAbortIn(path)
   197			return 0, fmt.Errorf("conflicts — wt rebase --continue")
   198		}
   199		return ab.Behind, nil
   200	}
   201	
   202	// dashFastForwardBase fast-forwards the base-branch worktree from its remote.
   203	// Mirrors the CLI's rebaseBaseBranch but without any interactive prompts: we
   204	// already bailed on dirty in dashRebase, so this just fetches and merges.
   205	func dashFastForwardBase(ctx *cmdContext, path string) (int, error) {
   206		if err := git.Fetch(ctx.Config.Remote, ctx.Config.BaseBranch); err != nil {
   207			return 0, fmt.Errorf("fetch failed: %w", err)
   208		}
   209		remoteRef := ctx.Config.Remote + "/" + ctx.Config.BaseBranch
   210		ab, err := git.GetAheadBehindIn(path, remoteRef)
   211		if err != nil {
   212			return 0, err
   213		}
   214		if ab.Behind == 0 {
   215			return 0, nil // up to date
   216		}
   217		if err := git.MergeFFIn(path, remoteRef); err != nil {
   218			return 0, fmt.Errorf("fast-forward failed: %w", err)
   219		}
   220		return ab.Behind, nil
   221	}
   222	
   223	// gatherCommitDetail loads full metadata + files for one commit. Wraps
   224	// git.CommitDetailIn and adapts the result into TUI-layer types.
   225	func gatherCommitDetail(worktreePath, hash string) (tui.DashCommitDetail, error) {
   226		raw, err := git.CommitDetailIn(worktreePath, hash)
   227		if err != nil {
   228			return tui.DashCommitDetail{}, err
   229		}
   230		d := tui.DashCommitDetail{
   231			Hash:    raw.Hash,
   232			Author:  raw.Author,
   233			Date:    raw.Date,
   234			Subject: raw.Subject,
   235			Body:    raw.Body,
   236		}
   237		for _, f := range raw.Files {
   238			d.Files = append(d.Files, tui.DashCommitFile{
   239				Status: f.Status,
   240				Path:   f.Path,
   241				Adds:   f.Adds,
   242				Dels:   f.Dels,
   243			})
   244		}
   245		return d, nil
   246	}
   247	
   248	// firstParagraph returns the first content paragraph of a PR body, skipping
   249	// leading markdown headers ("## Summary" etc.). Many PR templates start with a
   250	// "## Summary" heading followed by the actual content — we want the content,
   251	// not the heading.
   252	//
   253	// Returns "" if the body is empty or only contains headings.
   254	func firstParagraph(body string) string {
   255		for {
   256			body = strings.TrimSpace(body)
   257			if body == "" {
   258				return ""
   259			}
   260			// Leading line is a markdown header — peel it off and look at what
   261			// follows. Loop to handle stacked headers like "## Summary\n### Subsection".
   262			if strings.HasPrefix(body, "#") {
   263				nl := strings.IndexByte(body, '\n')
   264				if nl < 0 {
   265					return ""
   266				}
   267				body = body[nl+1:]
   268				continue
   269			}
   270			break
   271		}
   272		if idx := strings.Index(body, "\n\n"); idx >= 0 {
   273			body = body[:idx]
   274		}
   275		return strings.TrimSpace(body)
   276	}
   277	
   278	// gatherDashItems collects worktree + PR data and converts to TUI items.
   279	// Reuses the existing list helpers so dash and list stay in sync.
   280	func gatherDashItems(ctx *cmdContext, cwd string) ([]tui.DashItem, error) {
   281		worktrees, err := git.ListWorktrees()
   282		if err != nil {
   283			return nil, err
   284		}
   285	
   286		infos, branches := collectWorktreeInfos(ctx, cwd, worktrees)
   287	
   288		var openPRs, mergedPRs, closedPRs []github.PR
   289		if github.IsAvailable() {
   290			openPRs, mergedPRs, closedPRs, _ = fetchPRData(branches)
   291		}
   292	
   293		staleThreshold := ctx.Config.EffectiveStaleThreshold()
   294	
   295		items := make([]tui.DashItem, 0, len(infos))
   296		for _, info := range infos {
   297			isBase := ctx.isBaseBranch(info.Branch)
   298	
   299			item := tui.DashItem{
   300				Path:       info.Path,
   301				ShortName:  info.ShortName,
   302				Branch:     info.Branch,
   303				IsCurrent:  info.IsCurrent,
   304				IsBase:     isBase,
   305				Age:        info.Age,
   306				Behind:     info.Behind,

   168	// dashRebase syncs a worktree with its upstream. For feature branches that
   169	// means rebasing onto the configured base branch; for the base-branch worktree
   170	// itself it means fast-forwarding from the remote (since rebasing the base
   171	// onto itself is meaningless). Async-safe for use from the dashboard's
   172	// tea.Cmd: never prompts, never auto-stashes, aborts cleanly on conflict.
   173	// Returns the number of commits applied and an error describing why the
   174	// operation didn't proceed (dirty, conflicts, etc.).
   175	func dashRebase(ctx *cmdContext, path, branch string) (int, error) {
   176		if git.HasChangesIn(path) {
   177			return 0, fmt.Errorf("uncommitted changes")
   178		}
   179	
   180		if ctx.isBaseBranch(branch) {
   181			return dashFastForwardBase(ctx, path)
   182		}
   183	
   184		// Fetch the base ref so the rebase target is current. Failure here is
   185		// non-fatal — fall through to rebase against whatever's local.
   186		_ = git.Fetch(ctx.Config.Remote, ctx.Config.BaseBranch)
   187	
   188		ab, err := git.GetAheadBehindIn(path, ctx.baseRef())
   189		if err != nil {
   190			return 0, err
   191		}
   192		if ab.Behind == 0 {
   193			return 0, nil // up to date
   194		}
   195		if err := git.RebaseIn(path, ctx.baseRef()); err != nil {
   196			git.RebaseAbortIn(path)
   197			return 0, fmt.Errorf("conflicts — wt rebase --continue")
   198		}
   199		return ab.Behind, nil
   200	}
   201	
   202	// dashFastForwardBase fast-forwards the base-branch worktree from its remote.
   203	// Mirrors the CLI's rebaseBaseBranch but without any interactive prompts: we
   204	// already bailed on dirty in dashRebase, so this just fetches and merges.
   205	func dashFastForwardBase(ctx *cmdContext, path string) (int, error) {
   206		if err := git.Fetch(ctx.Config.Remote, ctx.Config.BaseBranch); err != nil {
   207			return 0, fmt.Errorf("fetch failed: %w", err)
   208		}
   209		remoteRef := ctx.Config.Remote + "/" + ctx.Config.BaseBranch
   210		ab, err := git.GetAheadBehindIn(path, remoteRef)
   211		if err != nil {
   212			return 0, err
   213		}
   214		if ab.Behind == 0 {
   215			return 0, nil // up to date
   216		}
   217		if err := git.MergeFFIn(path, remoteRef); err != nil {
   218			return 0, fmt.Errorf("fast-forward failed: %w", err)
   219		}
   220		return ab.Behind, nil
   221	}

   248	// firstParagraph returns the first content paragraph of a PR body, skipping
   249	// leading markdown headers ("## Summary" etc.). Many PR templates start with a
   250	// "## Summary" heading followed by the actual content — we want the content,
   251	// not the heading.
   252	//
   253	// Returns "" if the body is empty or only contains headings.
   254	func firstParagraph(body string) string {
   255		for {
   256			body = strings.TrimSpace(body)
   257			if body == "" {
   258				return ""
   259			}
   260			// Leading line is a markdown header — peel it off and look at what
   261			// follows. Loop to handle stacked headers like "## Summary\n### Subsection".
   262			if strings.HasPrefix(body, "#") {
   263				nl := strings.IndexByte(body, '\n')
   264				if nl < 0 {
   265					return ""
   266				}
   267				body = body[nl+1:]
   268				continue
   269			}
   270			break
   271		}
   272		if idx := strings.Index(body, "\n\n"); idx >= 0 {
   273			body = body[:idx]
   274		}
   275		return strings.TrimSpace(body)
   276	}

   278	// gatherDashItems collects worktree + PR data and converts to TUI items.
   279	// Reuses the existing list helpers so dash and list stay in sync.
   280	func gatherDashItems(ctx *cmdContext, cwd string) ([]tui.DashItem, error) {
   281		worktrees, err := git.ListWorktrees()
   282		if err != nil {
   283			return nil, err
   284		}
   285	
   286		infos, branches := collectWorktreeInfos(ctx, cwd, worktrees)
   287	
   288		var openPRs, mergedPRs, closedPRs []github.PR
   289		if github.IsAvailable() {
   290			openPRs, mergedPRs, closedPRs, _ = fetchPRData(branches)
   291		}
   292	
   293		staleThreshold := ctx.Config.EffectiveStaleThreshold()
   294	
   295		items := make([]tui.DashItem, 0, len(infos))
   296		for _, info := range infos {
   297			isBase := ctx.isBaseBranch(info.Branch)
   298	
   299			item := tui.DashItem{
   300				Path:       info.Path,
   301				ShortName:  info.ShortName,
   302				Branch:     info.Branch,
   303				IsCurrent:  info.IsCurrent,
   304				IsBase:     isBase,
   305				Age:        info.Age,
   306				Behind:     info.Behind,
   307				Ahead:      info.Ahead,
   308				DirtyCount: info.DirtyCount,
   309			}
   310	
   311			if !isBase {
   312				openPR := github.FindPRForBranch(openPRs, info.Branch)
   313				mergedPR := github.FindPRForBranch(mergedPRs, info.Branch)
   314				closedPR := github.FindPRForBranch(closedPRs, info.Branch)
   315	
   316				daysAgo := git.WorktreeAgeDays(info.Path)
   317				item.StaleDimmed = daysAgo >= staleThreshold && openPR == nil
   318	
   319				// Unpushed commits are the canonical data-loss signal for close —
   320				// fetch for every non-base worktree, not just ones with an open PR.
   321				// Cheap call (single rev-list --count); returns 0 if there's no
   322				// upstream so no need to special-case.
   323				item.Unpushed = git.UnpushedCountIn(info.Path)
   324	
   325				switch {
   326				case openPR != nil:
   327					rs := openPR.GetReviewSummary()
   328					cs := openPR.GetCISummary()
   329					item.PR = &tui.DashPR{
   330						Number: openPR.Number,
   331						State:  "open",
   332						Review: tui.DashReview{Approved: rs.Approved, Changes: rs.Changes, Pending: rs.Pending},
   333						CI:     tui.DashCI{Pass: cs.Pass, Fail: cs.Fail, Pending: cs.Pending, Total: cs.Total},
   334					}
   335				case mergedPR != nil:
   336					item.PR = &tui.DashPR{Number: mergedPR.Number, State: "merged"}
   337				case closedPR != nil:
   338					item.PR = &tui.DashPR{Number: closedPR.Number, State: "closed"}
   339				}
   340			}
   341	
   342			items = append(items, item)
   343		}
   344	
   345		return items, nil
   346	}

     9	var shellCmd = &cobra.Command{
    10		Use:   "init-shell <shell>",
    11		Short: "Print shell integration wrapper",
    12		Long: `Print a shell wrapper function that enables 'cd' integration.
    13	
    14	Add to your shell config:
    15	  Fish:  wt init-shell fish | source
    16	  Bash:  eval "$(wt init-shell bash)"
    17	  Zsh:   eval "$(wt init-shell zsh)"
    18

    20	need to change directory write the target path to that file, and
    21	the wrapper reads it after the command exits.`,
    22		Args:      cobra.ExactArgs(1),
    23		ValidArgs: []string{"fish", "bash", "zsh"},

    25	}

    29	}

    31	func runShell(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
    32		switch args[0] {
    33		case "fish":
    34			fmt.Print(fishWrapper)
    35		case "bash":
    36			fmt.Print(bashWrapper)
    37		case "zsh":
    38			fmt.Print(zshWrapper)

    40			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported shell: %s (use fish, bash, or zsh)", args[0])
    41		}
    42		return nil
    43	}
    44	
    45	const fishWrapper = `# wt shell integration (fish)
    46	# Add to ~/.config/fish/config.fish:
    47	#   wt init-shell fish | source
    48	
    49	function wt --wraps wt --description "Git worktree manager"
    50	    set -l cdfile (mktemp -t wt-cd.XXXXXXXX)
    51	    or begin
    52	        command wt $argv
    53	        return $status
    54	    end
    55	    WT_CD_FILE=$cdfile command wt $argv
    56	    set -l exit_code $status
    57	    if test -s $cdfile
    58	        read -l target < $cdfile
    59	        and cd $target
    60	    end
    61	    rm -f $cdfile
    62	    return $exit_code
    63	end
    64	
    65	# Completions are handled by cobra's built-in fish completion.
    66	# Generate with: wt completion fish | source
    67	`
    68	
    69	const bashWrapper = `# wt shell integration (bash)
    70	# Add to ~/.bashrc:
    71	#   eval "$(wt init-shell bash)"
    72	
    73	wt() {
    74	    local cdfile _wt_prev_trap
    75	    cdfile=$(mktemp -t wt-cd.XXXXXXXX) || {
    76	        command wt "$@"
    77	        return $?
    78	    }
    79	    _wt_prev_trap=$(trap -p EXIT 2>/dev/null)
    80	    trap 'rm -f "$cdfile"' EXIT
    81	    WT_CD_FILE="$cdfile" command wt "$@"
    82	    local exit_code=$?
    83	    if [ -s "$cdfile" ]; then
    84	        cd "$(cat "$cdfile")" || true
    85	    fi
    86	    rm -f "$cdfile"
    87	    if [ -n "$_wt_prev_trap" ]; then
    88	        eval "$_wt_prev_trap"
    89	    else
    90	        trap - EXIT
    91	    fi
    92	    return $exit_code
    93	}
    94	
    95	# Generate completions with: eval "$(wt completion bash)"
    96	`
    97	
    98	const zshWrapper = `# wt shell integration (zsh)
    99	# Add to ~/.zshrc:
   100	#   eval "$(wt init-shell zsh)"
   101	
   102	wt() {
   103	    local cdfile
   104	    cdfile=$(mktemp -t wt-cd.XXXXXXXX) || {
   105	        command wt "$@"
   106	        return $?
   107	    }
   108	    # In zsh, an EXIT trap set inside a function fires when the function
   109	    # returns and leaves the caller's EXIT trap alone.
   110	    trap "rm -f ${(q)cdfile}" EXIT
   111	    WT_CD_FILE="$cdfile" command wt "$@"
   112	    local exit_code=$?
   113	    if [ -s "$cdfile" ]; then
   114	        cd "$(cat "$cdfile")" || true
   115	    fi
   116	    return $exit_code
   117	}
   118	
   119	# Generate completions with: eval "$(wt completion zsh)"
   120	`

1	// Package tui contains BubbleTea-powered interactive screens.
     2	//
     3	// Each screen is invoked by a command in internal/cmd via a Run* entrypoint
     4	// that takes plain Go data, runs the model, and returns the user's decision.
     5	// Business logic stays in internal/cmd — the TUI is purely a picker/dashboard.
     6	package tui
     7	
     8	import (
     9		"fmt"
    10		"path/filepath"
    11		"strings"
    12	
    13		tea "charm.land/bubbletea/v2"
    14		"charm.land/lipgloss/v2"
    15	)
    16	
    17	// PruneItem describes one stale worktree presented to the user.
    18	type PruneItem struct {
    19		Path   string
    20		Branch string
    21		Reason string
    22	}
    23	
    24	// PruneResult is what the picker returns to the caller.
    25	// When Cancelled is true, Selected is empty and the caller should abort.
    26	type PruneResult struct {
    27		Cancelled bool
    28		Selected  []int
    29	}
    30	
    31	// RunPrunePicker presents a multi-select picker over the given items and
    32	// returns the user's selection. All items start selected — prune already
    33	// curates the list to merged/closed PRs, so opt-out matches intent better
    34	// than opt-in.
    35	func RunPrunePicker(items []PruneItem) (PruneResult, error) {
    36		if len(items) == 0 {
    37			return PruneResult{}, nil
    38		}
    39	
    40		selected := make([]bool, len(items))
    41		for i := range selected {
    42			selected[i] = true
    43		}
    44	
    45		m := pruneModel{items: items, selected: selected, width: 80}
    46		final, err := tea.NewProgram(m).Run()
    47		if err != nil {
    48			return PruneResult{}, err
    49		}
    50	
    51		pm := final.(pruneModel)
    52		if pm.cancelled {
    53			return PruneResult{Cancelled: true}, nil
    54		}
    55	
    56		var indices []int
    57		for i, s := range pm.selected {
    58			if s {
    59				indices = append(indices, i)
    60			}
    61		}
    62		return PruneResult{Selected: indices}, nil
    63	}
    64	
    65	type pruneModel struct {
    66		items     []PruneItem
    67		selected  []bool
    68		cursor    int
    69		width     int
    70		cancelled bool
    71		done      bool
    72	}
    73	
    74	var (
    75		styleCursor = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("11")).Bold(true)
    76		styleCheck  = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("10"))
    77		styleName   = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("11"))
    78		styleDim    = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("8"))
    79	)
    80	
    81	func (m pruneModel) Init() tea.Cmd { return nil }
    82	
    83	func (m pruneModel) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    84		switch msg := msg.(type) {
    85		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
    86			m.width = msg.Width
    87		case tea.KeyPressMsg:
    88			switch msg.String() {
    89			case "ctrl+c", "q", "esc":
    90				m.cancelled = true
    91				m.done = true
    92				return m, tea.Quit
    93			case "up", "k":
    94				if m.cursor > 0 {
    95					m.cursor--
    96				}
    97			case "down", "j":
    98				if m.cursor < len(m.items)-1 {
    99					m.cursor++
   100				}
   101			case "space", "x":
   102				m.selected[m.cursor] = !m.selected[m.cursor]
   103			case "a":
   104				allOn := true
   105				for _, s := range m.selected {
   106					if !s {
   107						allOn = false
   108						break
   109					}
   110				}
   111				for i := range m.selected {
   112					m.selected[i] = !allOn
   113				}
   114			case "enter":
   115				m.done = true
   116				return m, tea.Quit
   117			}
   118		}
   119		return m, nil
   120	}
   121	
   122	func (m pruneModel) View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.render()) }
   123	
   124	func (m pruneModel) render() string {
   125		if m.done {
   126			return ""
   127		}
   128	
   129		var b strings.Builder
   130		rule := strings.Repeat("─", min(m.width-4, 60))
   131	
   132		b.WriteString("\n")
   133		b.WriteString("  " + styleDim.Render("Stale worktrees") + "\n")
   134		b.WriteString("  " + styleDim.Render(rule) + "\n")
   135	
   136		selectedCount := 0
   137		for _, s := range m.selected {
   138			if s {
   139				selectedCount++
   140			}
   141		}
   142	
   143		for i, it := range m.items {
   144			cursor := "  "
   145			if i == m.cursor {
   146				cursor = styleCursor.Render(" ▸")
   147			}
   148	
   149			check := styleDim.Render("○")
   150			if m.selected[i] {
   151				check = styleCheck.Render("●")
   152			}
   153	
   154			short := filepath.Base(it.Path)
   155			nameRendered := styleName.Render(short)
   156			if !m.selected[i] {
   157				nameRendered = styleDim.Render(short)
   158			}
   159	
   160			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s %s %s  %s\n",
   161				cursor, check, nameRendered, styleDim.Render(it.Reason))
   162			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "       %s\n", styleDim.Render(it.Branch))
   163		}
   164	
   165		b.WriteString("  " + styleDim.Render(rule) + "\n")
   166		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %s\n",
   167			styleDim.Render(fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d selected   ↑↓ move · space toggle · a all · enter apply · q cancel",
   168				selectedCount, len(m.items))))
   169		return b.String()
   170	}

   109	// DashConfig bundles the data sources the dashboard needs. The TUI layer is
   110	// kept independent of git/github by taking these as callbacks from the cmd layer.
   111	type DashConfig struct {
   112		// Initial is rendered immediately at startup. Re-populated by Gather thereafter.
   113		Initial []DashItem
   114		// Gather is invoked on each refresh tick (and manual `r`) to repopulate the list.
   115		Gather func() ([]DashItem, error)
   116		// Close removes a worktree and (optionally) its branch. Pass nil to disable
   117		// the in-dashboard `c` action. Called for any close — risky or safe; the
   118		// dashboard handles risk-confirmation before invoking this.
   119		Close func(path, branch string) error
   120		// FetchDetail returns the bottom-panel detail for a single worktree.
   121		// Invoked lazily when the cursor lands on a row whose detail isn't cached,
   122		// and again on each refresh tick for the focused row so live state (CI, etc.)
   123		// stays current. Pass nil to disable the detail panel.
   124		FetchDetail func(item DashItem) (DashDetail, error)
   125		// FetchCommitDetail returns full detail (subject, body, files) for one commit.
   126		// Invoked lazily when the commit cursor lands on a row whose detail isn't
   127		// cached. Pass nil to disable the commit-detail panel.
   128		FetchCommitDetail func(worktreePath, hash string) (DashCommitDetail, error)

   130		// it. Returns the number of commits rebased and an error on conflicts or
   131		// other failure modes. Skips dirty worktrees with an error rather than
   132		// auto-stashing (the dashboard isn't the right place for surprise stash
   133		// operations). Pass nil to disable the `r` / `R` actions.
   134		Rebase func(path, branch string) (commits int, err error)

   137	// RunDashboard launches the interactive worktree dashboard. The dashboard owns
   138	// the terminal until the user presses enter (select) or q/esc/ctrl+c (quit).
   139	func RunDashboard(cfg DashConfig) (DashResult, error) {
   140		final, err := tea.NewProgram(newDashModel(cfg)).Run()
   141		if err != nil {
   142			return DashResult{}, err
   143		}
   144	
   145		fm := final.(dashModel)
   146		if fm.switchTo != "" {
   147			return DashResult{SwitchTo: fm.switchTo}, nil
   148		}
   149		return DashResult{}, nil
   150	}

   152	func newDashModel(cfg DashConfig) dashModel {
   153		return dashModel{
   154			items:               cfg.Initial,
   155			gather:              cfg.Gather,
   156			close:               cfg.Close,
   157			fetchDetail:         cfg.FetchDetail,
   158			fetchCommitDetail:   cfg.FetchCommitDetail,
   159			rebase:              cfg.Rebase,
   160			closes:              map[string]*dashCloseState{},
   161			rebases:             map[string]*dashRebaseState{},
   162			details:             map[string]*dashDetailCache{},
   163			detailLoading:       map[string]bool{},
   164			commitDetails:       map[string]*dashCommitDetailCache{},
   165			commitDetailLoading: map[string]bool{},
   166			lastRefresh:         time.Now(),

1	// Package tui contains BubbleTea-powered interactive screens.
     2	//
     3	// Each screen is invoked by a command in internal/cmd via a Run* entrypoint
     4	// that takes plain Go data, runs the model, and returns the user's decision.
     5	// Business logic stays in internal/cmd — the TUI is purely a picker/dashboard.
     6	package tui
     7	
     8	import (
     9		"fmt"
    10		"path/filepath"
    11		"strings"
    12	
    13		tea "charm.land/bubbletea/v2"
    14		"charm.land/lipgloss/v2"
    15	)
    16	
    17	// PruneItem describes one stale worktree presented to the user.
    18	type PruneItem struct {
    19		Path   string
    20		Branch string
    21		Reason string
    22	}
    23	
    24	// PruneResult is what the picker returns to the caller.
    25	// When Cancelled is true, Selected is empty and the caller should abort.
    26	type PruneResult struct {
    27		Cancelled bool
    28		Selected  []int
    29	}
    30	
    31	// RunPrunePicker presents a multi-select picker over the given items and
    32	// returns the user's selection. All items start selected — prune already
    33	// curates the list to merged/closed PRs, so opt-out matches intent better
    34	// than opt-in.
    35	func RunPrunePicker(items []PruneItem) (PruneResult, error) {
    36		if len(items) == 0 {
    37			return PruneResult{}, nil
    38		}
    39	
    40		selected := make([]bool, len(items))
    41		for i := range selected {
    42			selected[i] = true
    43		}
    44	
    45		m := pruneModel{items: items, selected: selected, width: 80}
    46		final, err := tea.NewProgram(m).Run()
    47		if err != nil {
    48			return PruneResult{}, err
    49		}
    50	
    51		pm := final.(pruneModel)
    52		if pm.cancelled {
    53			return PruneResult{Cancelled: true}, nil
    54		}
    55	
    56		var indices []int
    57		for i, s := range pm.selected {
    58			if s {
    59				indices = append(indices, i)
    60			}
    61		}
    62		return PruneResult{Selected: indices}, nil
    63	}
    64	
    65	type pruneModel struct {
    66		items     []PruneItem
    67		selected  []bool
    68		cursor    int
    69		width     int
    70		cancelled bool
    71		done      bool
    72	}
    73	
    74	var (
    75		styleCursor = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("11")).Bold(true)
    76		styleCheck  = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("10"))
    77		styleName   = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("11"))
    78		styleDim    = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("8"))
    79	)
    80	
    81	func (m pruneModel) Init() tea.Cmd { return nil }
    82	
    83	func (m pruneModel) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    84		switch msg := msg.(type) {
    85		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
    86			m.width = msg.Width
    87		case tea.KeyPressMsg:
    88			switch msg.String() {
    89			case "ctrl+c", "q", "esc":
    90				m.cancelled = true
    91				m.done = true
    92				return m, tea.Quit
    93			case "up", "k":
    94				if m.cursor > 0 {
    95					m.cursor--
    96				}
    97			case "down", "j":
    98				if m.cursor < len(m.items)-1 {
    99					m.cursor++
   100				}
   101			case "space", "x":
   102				m.selected[m.cursor] = !m.selected[m.cursor]
   103			case "a":
   104				allOn := true
   105				for _, s := range m.selected {
   106					if !s {
   107						allOn = false
   108						break
   109					}
   110				}
   111				for i := range m.selected {
   112					m.selected[i] = !allOn
   113				}
   114			case "enter":
   115				m.done = true
   116				return m, tea.Quit
   117			}
   118		}
   119		return m, nil
   120	}
   121	
   122	func (m pruneModel) View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.render()) }
   123	
   124	func (m pruneModel) render() string {
   125		if m.done {
   126			return ""
   127		}
   128	
   129		var b strings.Builder
   130		rule := strings.Repeat("─", min(m.width-4, 60))
   131	
   132		b.WriteString("\n")
   133		b.WriteString("  " + styleDim.Render("Stale worktrees") + "\n")
   134		b.WriteString("  " + styleDim.Render(rule) + "\n")
   135	
   136		selectedCount := 0
   137		for _, s := range m.selected {
   138			if s {
   139				selectedCount++
   140			}
   141		}
   142	
   143		for i, it := range m.items {
   144			cursor := "  "
   145			if i == m.cursor {
   146				cursor = styleCursor.Render(" ▸")
   147			}
   148	
   149			check := styleDim.Render("○")
   150			if m.selected[i] {
   151				check = styleCheck.Render("●")
   152			}
   153	
   154			short := filepath.Base(it.Path)
   155			nameRendered := styleName.Render(short)
   156			if !m.selected[i] {
   157				nameRendered = styleDim.Render(short)
   158			}
   159	
   160			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s %s %s  %s\n",
   161				cursor, check, nameRendered, styleDim.Render(it.Reason))
   162			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "       %s\n", styleDim.Render(it.Branch))
   163		}
   164	
   165		b.WriteString("  " + styleDim.Render(rule) + "\n")
   166		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %s\n",
   167			styleDim.Render(fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d selected   ↑↓ move · space toggle · a all · enter apply · q cancel",
   168				selectedCount, len(m.items))))
   169		return b.String()
   170	}

  1172				lo.dirtyWidth, "Dirty",
  1173				lo.syncWidth, "Sync",

  1182				lo.ageWidth, "Commit",

  1317	// footerKeys returns the footer key hints, one styled string per key.
  1318	// r/R/c get a struck-through look when the cursor row can't take them
  1319	// (busy, base branch, or current worktree).
  1320	func footerKeys(m dashModel) []string {
  1321		keys := worktreeKeyHelp
  1322		enabled := map[string]bool{}
  1323		rLabel := "rebase"
  1324		if m.focus == focusCommits {
  1325			keys = commitKeyHelp
  1326		} else {
  1327			// cursor out of range only happens when items is empty — treat
  1328			// actions as disabled then.
  1329			var cur DashItem
  1330			rowExists := m.cursor >= 0 && m.cursor < len(m.items)
  1331			if rowExists {
  1332				cur = m.items[m.cursor]
  1333			}
  1334			busy := rowExists && m.rowBusy(cur.Path)
  1335			enabled["s"] = rowExists
  1336			enabled["r"] = rowExists && !busy
  1337			enabled["R"] = m.countRebaseTargets() > 0
  1338			enabled["c"] = rowExists && canClose(cur) && !busy
  1339			// Base-branch rows fast-forward from the remote rather than rebase.
  1340			if rowExists && cur.IsBase {
  1341				rLabel = "fast-forward"
  1342			}
  1343		}
  1344	
  1345		var parts []string
  1346		for _, k := range keys {
  1347			if !k.footer {
  1348				continue
  1349			}
  1350			label := k.label
  1351			if k.keys == "r" {
  1352				label = rLabel
  1353			}
  1354			text := k.keys + " " + label
  1355			if on, ok := enabled[k.keys]; ok && !on {
  1356				parts = append(parts, dStyleDisabled.Render(text))
  1357			} else {
  1358				parts = append(parts, dStyleDim.Render(text))
  1359			}
  1360		}
  1361		return parts
  1362	}

  1364	// layoutFooter wraps the key hints to width and puts status at the right
  1365	// edge of the last line, or on a line of its own when it doesn't fit.
  1366	func layoutFooter(parts []string, status string, width int) []string {
  1367		sep := dStyleDim.Render(" · ")
  1368		var lines []string
  1369		line := ""
  1370		for _, p := range parts {
  1371			switch {
  1372			case line == "":
  1373				line = p
  1374			case lipgloss.Width(line)+lipgloss.Width(sep)+lipgloss.Width(p) <= width:
  1375				line += sep + p
  1376			default:
  1377				lines = append(lines, line)
  1378				line = p
  1379			}
  1380		}
  1381		if status != "" {
  1382			if pad := width - lipgloss.Width(line) - lipgloss.Width(status); pad >= 2 {
  1383				line += strings.Repeat(" ", pad) + status
  1384			} else {
  1385				lines = append(lines, line)
  1386				line = status
  1387			}
  1388		}
  1389		return append(lines, line)
  1390	}

  1444

   890	// issueRefRe matches GitHub-style issue/PR references in free text (e.g. "#42"
   891	// in "Closes #42"). We don't try to be clever about preceded-by-letter cases
   892	// (foo#42); GitHub itself is lenient here.
   893	var issueRefRe = regexp.MustCompile(`#\d+`)
   894	
   895	// colorizeBody renders free-form text in dim while highlighting issue
   896	// references (`#123`) in blue. Used for PR bodies and commit bodies.
   897	func colorizeBody(s string) string {
   898		matches := issueRefRe.FindAllStringIndex(s, -1)
   899		if len(matches) == 0 {
   900			return dStyleDim.Render(s)
   901		}
   902		var b strings.Builder
   903		pos := 0
   904		for _, m := range matches {
   905			if m[0] > pos {
   906				b.WriteString(dStyleDim.Render(s[pos:m[0]]))
   907			}
   908			b.WriteString(dStyleBlue.Render(s[m[0]:m[1]]))
   909			pos = m[1]
   910		}
   911		if pos < len(s) {
   912			b.WriteString(dStyleDim.Render(s[pos:]))
   913		}
   914		return b.String()
   915	}

   917	// styleForAge returns a foreground style based on how recent a commit is.
   918	// Fresh worktrees (hours/minutes) pop in green; normal age (days) is default;
   919	// older (weeks/months/years) stays dim — same as the stale-row behavior.
   920	func styleForAge(age string) lipgloss.Style {
   921		if age == "" {
   922			return dStyleDim
   923		}
   924		var unit string
   925		for i, c := range age {
   926			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
   927				unit = age[i:]
   928				break
   929			}
   930		}
   931		switch unit {
   932		case "s", "m", "h":
   933			return dStyleGreen
   934		case "d":
   935			return dStylePlain
   936		default:
   937			return dStyleDim
   938		}
   939	}

   941	// stylesForFilePath colors paths by their semantic category. Tests stand out
   942	// in magenta so churn there is distinguishable from real source changes;
   943	// configs are cyan; docs are dim; everything else (code) uses the default.
   944	func styleForFilePath(path string) lipgloss.Style {
   945		lower := strings.ToLower(path)
   946		// Test / spec files
   947		base := lower
   948		if i := strings.LastIndex(lower, "/"); i >= 0 {
   949			base = lower[i+1:]
   950		}
   951		if strings.Contains(base, "test") || strings.Contains(base, "spec") {
   952			return dStyleMagenta
   953		}
   954		// Docs
   955		switch {
   956		case strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".md"),
   957			strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".txt"),
   958			strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".rst"):
   959			return dStyleDim
   960		}
   961		// Config
   962		switch {
   963		case strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".toml"),
   964			strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".yaml"),
   965			strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".yml"),
   966			strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".json"),
   967			strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".ini"),
   968			strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".env"):
   969			return dStyleCyan
   970		}
   971		return dStylePlain
   972	}

  1000	// dashLayout is the computed column geometry for one render pass. Computed
  1001	// once per View() from m.width + the current items so every renderer sees the
  1002	// same dimensions. termWidth=0 (before the first WindowSizeMsg) is handled by
  1003	// falling back to an 80-col baseline in computeLayout.
  1004	type dashLayout struct {
  1005		mode         layoutMode
  1006		termWidth    int
  1007		contentWidth int // total visible row width, including the leading "  " indent
  1008		nameWidth    int
  1009		branchWidth  int
  1010		ageWidth     int
  1011		dirtyWidth   int
  1012		syncWidth    int
  1013		prWidth      int
  1014		reviewWidth  int
  1015		ciWidth      int
  1016		statusWidth  int // used only when mode == layoutNarrow
  1017	}
  1018	
  1019	// tailWidth is the width of the trailing PR/Review/CI cluster (full mode) or
  1020	// the Status cell (narrow mode). Used by per-row overlays (prune, rebase) so
  1021	// they fill the same horizontal slot.
  1022	func (l dashLayout) tailWidth() int {
  1023		if l.mode == layoutNarrow {
  1024			return l.statusWidth
  1025		}
  1026		return l.prWidth + 1 + l.reviewWidth + 1 + l.ciWidth
  1027	}

  1029	// ruleWidth is the number of "─" characters that fit between the leading
  1030	// "  " margin and the row's right edge. Used for dividers and for aligning
  1031	// the footer's right-edge status.
  1032	func (l dashLayout) ruleWidth() int { return l.contentWidth - 2 }
  1033	
  1034	// detailWidth is the width budget passed into the detail/commit-detail
  1035	// panels — same as ruleWidth so panel content lines up under the dividers.

  1038	// minNarrowWidth returns the smallest terminal width that fits the narrow
  1039	// layout for the given name column — used by the tiny-mode hint message.
  1040	func minNarrowWidth(nameWidth int) int {
  1041		// "  " + cursor(2) + current(2) + name + "  " + minBranch + " " + age + " "
  1042		// + dirty + " " + sync + " " + status
  1043		return 2 + 2 + 2 + nameWidth + 2 + colBranchMin + 1 + colAge + 1 + colDirty + 1 + colSync + 1 + colStatus
  1044	}
  1045	
  1046	// computeLayout chooses a mode and column widths for the given terminal size.
  1047	// Branch column flexes to consume any slack; PR/Review/CI collapse to a single
  1048	// Status column when there isn't enough room. termWidth <= 0 (initial render
  1049	// before WindowSizeMsg) falls back to 80 columns — a conservative default
  1050	// that fits in tmux, vsplit panes, and most "default" terminal sizes.
  1051	func computeLayout(items []DashItem, termWidth int) dashLayout {
  1052		nameWidth := 8
  1053		for _, it := range items {
  1054			nameWidth = max(nameWidth, lipgloss.Width(it.ShortName))
  1055		}
  1056	
  1057		if termWidth <= 0 {
  1058			termWidth = 80
  1059		}
  1060		avail := termWidth - 2 // leading "  " indent
  1061	
  1062		// Fixed widths excluding the branch column.
  1063		fixedFull := 2 + 2 + nameWidth + 2 + 1 + colAge + 1 + colDirty + 1 + colSync + 1 + (colPR + 1 + colReview + 1 + colCI)
  1064		fixedNarrow := 2 + 2 + nameWidth + 2 + 1 + colAge + 1 + colDirty + 1 + colSync + 1 + colStatus
  1065	
  1066		lo := dashLayout{
  1067			termWidth:   termWidth,
  1068			nameWidth:   nameWidth,
  1069			ageWidth:    colAge,
  1070			dirtyWidth:  colDirty,
  1071			syncWidth:   colSync,
  1072			prWidth:     colPR,
  1073			reviewWidth: colReview,
  1074			ciWidth:     colCI,
  1075			statusWidth: colStatus,
  1076		}

  1078		switch {

  1119		case n > ceiling:

  1121		}

``` █████ ▒▒███ █████ ███ █████ ███████ ▒▒███ ▒███▒▒███ ▒▒▒███▒ ▒███ ▒███ ▒███ ▒███ ▒▒███████████ ▒███ ███ ▒▒████▒████ ▒▒█████ ▒▒▒▒ ▒▒▒▒ ▒▒▒▒▒ ``` *Worktrees without the irk thees.* Git worktrees are the best way to work on multiple branches at the same time. No stashing, no context-switching, no waiting for dependencies to reinstall. Every branch gets its own directory, ready to go. But the built-in commands make it hard to love them. Creating a worktree means juggling `git worktree add`, `git checkout -b`, and a path you have to remember. Switching between them means typing out full directory paths. Figuring out which ones still have open PRs, or which ones were merged three weeks ago and are just sitting there, means checking GitHub manually. `wt` handles all of that. Create a worktree and branch in one command, or wrap an existing branch with `--from`. Switch without typing paths. Rebase and push with `wt submit`. PR status, CI checks, and code review show up right in your terminal, and when a PR merges, `wt prune` cleans everything up. It's a thin layer over git. No special repo format, no lock-in. Your worktrees and branches are normal git. `wt` just makes them easier to manage. Remove it and everything still works. Works without config. `wt list` pulls in PR status, CI, and code review from GitHub. Shell `cd` just works when you switch worktrees. ## How It Works ```sh wt new sidebar-card # Create worktree + branch, cd into it wt init # Copy files, run commands from .wt.toml # ...work on your feature... wt submit # Rebase onto main + push (offers to watch PR) wt list # See all worktrees with PR/CI/review status # ...PR gets merged on GitHub... wt prune # Clean up merged worktrees ``` ## Use Cases
Run multiple agent sessions in parallel You want two agents working on different tasks at the same time. If they share a branch, they'll overwrite each other's files and fight over `git status`. ```sh wt new auth-refactor --init # Agent 1 gets its own worktree wt new fix-pagination --init # Agent 2 gets a separate one ``` Each agent works in complete isolation — its own directory, its own branch, its own node_modules. `--init` copies `.env` files, installs dependencies, and sets up AI config (`.claude`, `.cursorrules`) automatically. When they're done, push each independently, then `wt watch` for updates as CI runs.
Fix a bug without derailing your current work You're deep in changes when you find an unrelated bug. The old way: stash your changes, make a new branch, fix the bug, switch back, pop the stash, and hope nothing broke (except your concentration). Or more likely, ignore it and tell yourself you'll fix it later. ```sh wt new hotfix # New worktree from main — your feature branch is untouched # ...fix the bug... wt submit # Rebase + push the fix wt switch - # Back to your feature, exactly where you left off (or even better, farm this out to an agent to preserve your focus too) ``` Same thing works for addressing PR review comments on a different branch — `wt switch` to it, make the changes, `wt submit`, `wt switch -` back.
Move work you started on the wrong branch You've been coding for 20 minutes before realizing you're on `main`. Or you started on `feature-a` but this really belongs in its own branch. ```sh wt move new-feature # Moves all uncommitted changes to another worktree ``` If the target doesn't exist, `wt move` offers to create it. It detects conflicts with files already modified in the target, cleans up the source after a successful move, and creates any missing directories. The manual alternative — copying files, checking for conflicts, running `git checkout .` and `git clean` — is tedious and error-prone.
Set up a new worktree without the boilerplate A new worktree is a bare directory. No `node_modules`, no `.env`, no generated files. Getting it into a working state means copying environment files, running the right install command, generating Prisma schemas, and setting up AI tool configs. Lots of manual effort relative to `git checkout -b`. ```sh wt init # Auto-detects and handles everything ``` With zero configuration, `wt init` detects your package manager from lockfiles, copies `.env` files from main, copies AI config directories, and runs install with the right frozen-lockfile flags. Support out of the box for `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun`, `npm`, `Go`, `Cargo`, `Bundler`, and `pip`. If you use Prisma, it finds your schema and generates. All of this is customizable in `.wt.toml` if the defaults aren't right.
Push and stop refreshing GitHub You push your branch and alt-tab to GitHub, refreshing until CI goes green and reviewers approve. If a check fails, you might not notice for 10 minutes. ```sh wt submit # Rebase onto main + push (force-with-lease) # "Watch PR status? [Y/n]" wt watch # Live terminal dashboard, polls every 15s ``` `wt watch` shows CI checks and review status in a live-updating table. When everything resolves — or something fails — you get a desktop notification and a terminal bell. No more tab-switching.
## Install **Homebrew:** ```sh brew install mvwi/tap/wt ``` **Go:** ```sh go install github.com/mvwi/wt/cmd/wt@latest ``` **Binary:** Download from [Releases](https://github.com/mvwi/wt/releases). ### Shell Setup `wt` needs a thin shell wrapper so it can `cd` into worktrees for you. Add one line to your shell config: **Fish** (`~/.config/fish/config.fish`): ```fish wt init-shell fish | source wt completion fish | source ``` **Bash** (`~/.bashrc`): ```bash eval "$(wt init-shell bash)" eval "$(wt completion bash)" ``` **Zsh** (`~/.zshrc`): ```zsh eval "$(wt init-shell zsh)" eval "$(wt completion zsh)" ``` ## Commands | Command | Aliases | Description | |---------|---------|-------------| | `wt` | | Show current worktree status (branch, sync, PR) | | `wt new ` | `create` | Create worktree with feature branch | | `wt init` | | Initialize worktree (auto-detects or uses config) | | `wt list` | `ls` | Show all worktrees with PR status | | `wt dash` | `dashboard` | Live worktree dashboard (TUI) | | `wt switch [name]` | `sw`, `cd`, `checkout`, `co` | Switch to a worktree (fzf picker if no args, `-` for previous) | | `wt rebase` | | Rebase current branch onto base branch (auto-installs deps if lockfile changed) | | `wt submit` | | Rebase + push to remote | | `wt move ` | `mv`, `teleport`, `tp` | Move uncommitted changes to another worktree | | `wt close [name]` | `rm` | Close and clean up a worktree | | `wt rename ` | `rn` | Rename worktree, branch, and remote | | `wt prune` | | Clean up stale worktrees (merged/closed PRs) | | `wt pull [name]` | | Pull a remote branch into a new worktree | | `wt pr ` | | Checkout a PR into a worktree | | `wt open [name]` | | Open PR in browser | | `wt watch [branch or PR]` | | Watch PR until mergeable or blocked | | `wt edit [name]` | | Open a worktree in your editor | | `wt prompt` | | Print a prompt segment for the current worktree (no network) | | `wt skill` | | Print a SKILL.md that teaches AI agents to use wt | | `wt feedback [message]` | | Open a GitHub issue for feedback | Run `wt --help` for detailed usage of any command. Worktrees live next to the repo, in `../wt-/`. `wt pr` works for PRs from forks too: they check out as `pr/-`, and wt prints how to push back to the fork. ### Global flags | Flag | Description | |------|-------------| | `--yes`, `-y` | Skip confirmation prompts (useful for scripts and agents). Never discards work: see `--force` | | `-C ` | Run as if started in `` | ### Notable command flags | Flag | Commands | Description | |------|----------|-------------| | `--force`, `-f` | `close`, `move` | Allow discarding uncommitted changes or unpushed commits. Without it, wt refuses (exit 1) when it can't ask | | `--run ""` | `new`, `pr`, `pull` | Run a command in the new worktree; wt exits with its code. E.g. `wt new fix-123 -i --run "claude 'fix issue 123'"` | | `--edit`, `-e` | `new`, `pr`, `pull` | Open the new worktree in your editor | | `--init`, `-i` | `new`, `pr`, `pull` | Run `wt init` after creating | | `--output json` | `list`, `new`, `pr`, `pull`, `switch`, `close`, `submit` | Machine-readable output. Only JSON goes to stdout, and wt never prompts | | `--dry-run` | `prune` | Preview what would be removed without removing anything | | `--all` | `rebase` | Rebase all worktrees at once | | `--merge` | `watch` | Auto-merge PR when ready | `wt edit` picks `$WT_EDITOR`, then `$VISUAL`, then the first of `cursor`, `code`, `zed` on your PATH. ### Prompt segment `wt prompt` prints something like `login-form ⇡2 ⇣5 #123 ✓` for the current worktree, and nothing in the main checkout. It reads local git refs plus a PR/CI cache that `wt list`, `wt dash` and `wt watch` refresh, so it never touches the network. Starship (`~/.config/starship.toml`): ```toml [custom.wt] command = "wt prompt" when = true format = "[$output]($style) " ``` Fish: add `echo -n (wt prompt)` to your `fish_prompt`. ## Configuration All fields are optional. Config is layered: **defaults -> global -> repo**, each layer only overrides what it sets. - **Global** (`~/.config/wt/config.toml`): applies to all repos - **Repo** (`.wt.toml` in repo root): overrides global for that repo
Config reference and examples ```toml # Base branch to create worktrees from and rebase onto. # Default: "main". Common alternatives: "staging", "develop" base_branch = "staging" # Git remote name. Default: "origin" remote = "origin" # Prefix for new branch names: "/". # Default: your git username's first name (e.g., "michael"). # Set to "" to disable prefixing entirely. branch_prefix = "michael" # Worktree directory naming. # Default: nested layout "wt-/" (e.g., "wt-myapp/sidebar"). # Set to override with flat layout: "" (e.g., "wt-" → "wt-sidebar"). worktree_prefix = "" # Days before a worktree with no open PR is flagged stale in `wt list`. # Default: 7 stale_threshold = 14 # Auto-run install command after rebase when lockfile changes. # Default: true auto_install = false [init] # Files to copy from the main worktree (if missing in the new worktree). # Without [init], auto-detected: .env, .env.local, .env.development, .env.test copy_files = [".env", ".env.local"] # Shell commands to run sequentially during init. # Without [init], auto-detected from lockfile: pnpm/yarn/npm/go/cargo/bundler commands = ["pnpm install", "npx prisma generate"] # Directories cloned from the main worktree before commands run, using # copy-on-write (APFS clonefile, or cp --reflink on Linux). A large # node_modules clones in well under a second; install then only fixes the diff. # Skipped with a note when the file system can't clone. clone_dirs = ["node_modules"] # Lines written into the worktree's env file (replaced if the key exists). # Templates: {index} {port} {name} {branch} {repo} env = { PORT = "{port}", COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME = "{repo}-{name}" } env_file = ".env" # default ``` **Hooks** run shell commands at points in a worktree's life. They run without being asked for, so wt reads them only from your global config (`~/.config/wt/config.toml`), never from a repo's `.wt.toml`. Otherwise any repo you clone could run code on `wt new`. wt warns when it skips `[hooks]` in `.wt.toml`. ```toml # ~/.config/wt/config.toml [hooks] # all repos # Run via sh -c. A failing pre_close stops the close; post_* failures only warn. post_new = ["tmux new-window -d -c \"$WT_PATH\" -n \"$WT_NAME\""] # cwd: new worktree (new, pr, pull) post_close = [] # cwd: main worktree [repos.myapp.hooks] # one repo pre_close = ["docker compose down"] # cwd: worktree being closed ``` **Running worktrees side by side.** Each worktree gets a stable `WT_INDEX` (main is 0, others take the lowest free number; it survives renames and frees up on close). `WT_PORT` is `port_base + WT_INDEX`. Init commands and hooks get `WT_NAME`, `WT_PATH`, `WT_BRANCH`, `WT_MAIN`, `WT_REPO`, `WT_INDEX` and `WT_PORT`, so two dev servers or two docker stacks don't collide. If a worktree has `.envrc`, `mise.toml`, `.mise.toml` or `.tool-versions`, wt reminds you to run `direnv allow` / `mise trust`. It never runs them for you. ### Global Config with Per-Repo Overrides Set everything in `~/.config/wt/config.toml` so you don't need to commit config to repos: ```toml # Defaults for all repos base_branch = "main" # Per-repo overrides (keyed by repo directory name) [repos.platform] base_branch = "staging" [repos.legacy-app] base_branch = "develop" branch_prefix = "fix" ``` Precedence: **defaults -> global -> global per-repo -> .wt.toml** A `.wt.toml` in a repo root always wins, but most users won't need one. ### Settings Reference | Setting | Default | Effect | |---------|---------|--------| | `base_branch` | `"main"` | Branch used for `wt new`, `wt rebase`, `wt submit` | | `remote` | `"origin"` | Remote for fetch/push operations | | `branch_prefix` | git username | New branches: `/` | | `worktree_prefix` | `"wt-/"` | Directory naming: nested `wt-/` | | `stale_threshold` | `7` | Days before worktree flagged stale in `wt list` | | `auto_install` | `true` | Run install after rebase when lockfile changes | | `port_base` | `3000` | `WT_PORT = port_base + WT_INDEX` | | `init.copy_files` | `[]` | Files copied from main worktree if missing | | `init.commands` | `[]` | Shell commands run during init | | `init.clone_dirs` | `[]` | Directories cloned copy-on-write from the main worktree | | `init.env` | `{}` | Key/template pairs written into `init.env_file` | | `init.env_file` | `".env"` | File that `init.env` writes to | | `hooks.post_new` | `[]` | Commands run after `new`, `pr`, `pull` (global config only) | | `hooks.pre_close` | `[]` | Commands run before `close`; failure aborts | | `hooks.post_close` | `[]` | Commands run after `close` |
## AI Tools `wt` works well with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, etc.) — agents with shell access can run `wt` commands directly. - `wt skill` prints a SKILL.md built from the command tree, so it can't go stale. Install it for Claude Code with `mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/wt && wt skill > ~/.claude/skills/wt/SKILL.md` - One agent per worktree: `wt new fix-123 -i --run "claude 'fix issue 123'"` - `--output json` on `list`, `new`, `pr`, `pull`, `switch`, `close` and `submit` prints only JSON to stdout and never prompts; a needed confirmation becomes an error - `wt list --output toon` outputs token-efficient worktree and PR status (~50% fewer tokens than JSON) - Commands emit `cta: cmd1 | cmd2` on stdout when piped (non-TTY), telling agents what to run next - `-y` never discards work. `wt close` refuses to drop uncommitted changes or unpushed commits without `--force`, so an agent can't lose work by accident - `wt init` auto-copies AI config (`.claude`, `.cursorrules`, `.cursor/rules`) to new worktrees ### LLM Instructions Add the following to your AI tool's instructions file so it knows to use `wt` instead of raw git commands for worktree operations. Copy the block below into your `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, or equivalent:
Copy-paste snippet ~~~markdown ## Worktree Management This project uses `wt` (git worktree manager). Use `wt` commands instead of raw `git worktree` or `git checkout -b` commands. Key commands: - `wt new ` — create a new worktree + branch (add `--init` to install deps and copy env files) - `wt switch ` — switch to another worktree (supports fuzzy matching) - `wt list` — show all worktrees with PR, CI, and review status - `wt rebase` — rebase current branch onto the base branch - `wt submit` — rebase + push to remote - `wt close [name]` — clean up a worktree when done - `wt prune` — remove worktrees whose PRs were merged or closed Use `wt submit` instead of `git push` — it rebases onto the base branch first and uses `--force-with-lease` for safety. Use `wt rebase` instead of `git rebase` — it handles fetching and knows the configured base branch. Use `wt new --init` to create fully set up worktrees with dependencies installed. Run `wt --help` for detailed usage of any command. ~~~
## Dependencies - **git** (required) - **gh** (GitHub CLI, optional): PR status in `wt list`, safety checks in `wt close`, remote rename in `wt rename`. Without it, `wt prune` falls back to branches merged into the base branch (it can't see squash merges) - **fzf** (optional): interactive picker in `wt switch` `wt` checks for new versions once daily and shows a notification when an update is available. ## License MIT

It never runs them for you. ### Global Config with Per-Repo Overrides Set everything in `~/.config/wt/config.toml` so you don't need to commit config to repos: ```toml # Defaults for all repos base_branch = "main" # Per-repo overrides (keyed by repo directory name) [repos.platform] base_branch = "staging" [repos.legacy-app] base_branch = "develop" branch_prefix = "fix" ``` Precedence: **defaults -> global -> global per-repo -> .wt.toml** A `.wt.toml` in a repo root always wins, but most users won't need one. ### Settings Reference | Setting | Default | Effect | |---------|---------|--------| | `base_branch` | `"main"` | Branch used for `wt new`, `wt rebase`, `wt submit` | | `remote` | `"origin"` | Remote for fetch/push operations | | `branch_prefix` | git username | New branches: `/` | | `worktree_prefix` | `"wt-/"` | Directory naming: nested `wt-/` | | `stale_threshold` | `7` | Days before worktree flagged stale in `wt list` | | `auto_install` | `true` | Run install after rebase when lockfile changes | | `port_base` | `3000` | `WT_PORT = port_base + WT_INDEX` | | `init.copy_files` | `[]` | Files copied from main worktree if missing | | `init.commands` | `[]` | Shell commands run during init | | `init.clone_dirs` | `[]` | Directories cloned copy-on-write from the main worktree | | `init.env` | `{}` | Key/template pairs written into `init.env_file` | | `init.env_file` | `".env"` | File that `init.env` writes to | | `hooks.post_new` | `[]` | Commands run after `new`, `pr`, `pull` (global config only) | | `hooks.pre_close` | `[]` | Commands run before `close`; failure aborts | | `hooks.post_close` | `[]` | Commands run after `close` |
## AI Tools `wt` works well with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, etc.) — agents with shell access can run `wt` commands directly. - `wt skill` prints a SKILL.md built from the command tree, so it can't go stale. Install it for Claude Code with `mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/wt && wt skill > ~/.claude/skills/wt/SKILL.md` - One agent per worktree: `wt new fix-123 -i --run "claude 'fix issue 123'"` - `--output json` on `list`, `new`, `pr`, `pull`, `switch`, `close` and `submit` prints only JSON to stdout and never prompts; a needed confirmation becomes an error - `wt list --output toon` outputs token-efficient worktree and PR status (~50% fewer tokens than JSON) - Commands emit `cta: cmd1 | cmd2` on stdout when piped (non-TTY), telling agents what to run next - `-y` never discards work. `wt close` refuses to drop uncommitted changes or unpushed commits without `--force`, so an agent can't lose work by accident - `wt init` auto-copies AI config (`.claude`, `.cursorrules`, `.cursor/rules`) to new worktrees ### LLM Instructions Add the following to your AI tool's instructions file so it knows to use `wt` instead of raw git commands for worktree operations. Copy the block below into your `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, or equivalent:
Copy-paste snippet ~~~markdown ## Worktree Management This project uses `wt` (git worktree manager). Use `wt` commands instead of raw `git worktree` or `git checkout -b` commands. Key commands: - `wt new ` — create a new worktree + branch (add `--init` to install deps and copy env files) - `wt switch ` — switch to another worktree (supports fuzzy matching) - `wt list` — show all worktrees with PR, CI, and review status - `wt rebase` — rebase current branch onto the base branch - `wt submit` — rebase + push to remote - `wt close [name]` — clean up a worktree when done - `wt prune` — remove worktrees whose PRs were merged or closed Use `wt submit` instead of `git push` — it rebases onto the base branch first and uses `--force-with-lease` for safety. Use `wt rebase` instead of `git rebase` — it handles fetching and knows the configured base branch. Use `wt new --init` to create fully set up worktrees with dependencies installed. Run `wt --help` for detailed usage of any command. ~~~
## Dependencies - **git** (required) - **gh** (GitHub CLI, optional): PR status in `wt list`, safety checks in `wt close`, remote rename in `wt rename`. Without it, `wt prune` falls back to branches merged into the base branch (it can't see squash merges) - **fzf** (optional): interactive picker in `wt switch` `wt` checks for new versions once daily and shows a notification when an update is available. ## License MIT

content.text:
I found and fixed eight real bugs, one of which lost data, plus a batch of smaller cleanups. Nothing is committed. Tests, vet and lint pass, and I reproduced the first six bugs in a scratch repo before fixing them, then confirmed each fix there.

## Fixed

**Bugs**
- **`wt move` deleted files.** Any changed file with a space or non-ASCII character in its name was dropped from the source and never copied. Git quotes such paths unless asked not to, so the status parser now uses `-z`.
- **`wt switch -` never worked across worktrees.** The previous-worktree marker was written to one worktree's git dir and read from another's. It now lives in the shared git dir.
- **`wt rebase --all` moved `main` to the base branch.** With `base_branch = "staging"`, a worktree on `main` was fast-forwarded to `origin/staging`. The dashboard's fast-forward had the same fault.
- **`wt close` and `wt rename` failed from a subdirectory.** Both treated the current directory as the worktree root.
- **`wt switch feat` could cd into a plain directory.** With a `feat/foo` worktree, `feat` matched as an exact hit. Matching now uses the worktree list, and `foo` resolves to `feat/foo` without the fuzzy warning.
- **`wt prune` could remove a worktree with an open PR.** A reused branch name with an old merged or closed PR counted as stale.
- **`wt init` made copied files world-readable.** A `0600` `.env` came out `0644`.
- **Bare `wt` never showed review or CI status.** It fetched only the PR number, so those lines were dead.

**Smaller fixes**
- Dashboard diff stats counted the base branch's new commits as deletions, and paths with spaces were cut short.
- A long commit subject in the dashboard could be cut inside a colour code.
- `wt watch <branch>` now works for branches that aren't checked out, as its help says.
- `wt list --output <unknown>` now errors instead of printing the table.
- Bun's text lockfile `bun.lock` is detected.
- The dashboard's conflict message no longer suggests `--continue` after it has aborted the rebase.

**Efficiency and dead code**
- Every command ran `git worktree list` three times at startup; now once.
- Ahead/behind takes one git call instead of two.
- Removed four unused functions and two duplicated helpers.

**Docs**
- README, the root help and the Homebrew caveat still said `wt new` changes directory. It stopped doing that in commit `28edd43`.
- Corrected stale comments and `wt switch` help, and updated `CLAUDE.md`.

## For you to review

- **Unpushed check has a hole.** A branch with no upstream counts as zero unpushed commits, so `wt close` and the dashboard's `c` delete it without asking. Default git config sets an upstream on `wt new`, so this only hits users with `branch.autoSetupMerge=false`.
- **`wt prune` ignores unpushed commits.** It checks only for uncommitted changes before force-deleting the branch.
- **Hooks are skipped by `wt prune` and the dashboard close.** Only `wt close` runs `pre_close` and `post_close`.
- **`wt rename` recreates the PR**, which loses reviews and comments. GitHub's branch-rename API keeps the PR.
- **`wt open` can't open merged or closed PRs**, and its "PR is closed" warning can never fire.
- **`wt init` exits 0 when a step fails**, so `wt new -i --run` carries on regardless.
- **`wt new --from #123` accepts closed PRs**; `wt pr 123` rejects them.
- **`wt list` is slower than its help claims.** All git calls run in series before the "instant" first phase prints.
- **Dashboard `R` fetches once per worktree**, all at the same time.
- **Auto-install after rebase looks for the lockfile in the current directory**, so it misses from a subdirectory.
- **`wt -C dir prompt` still triggers the update check**, because the check reads the first argument only.
- **The update-check cache sits in the config dir**; the prompt cache uses the cache dir.
- **`dist/` and `./wt` are stale local builds**, both gitignored. `make clean` removes them.

Not verified: the dashboard changes in a live terminal, and the paths that need an authenticated `gh` (the bare `wt` PR line, the prune open-PR check). Those compile and pass tests only.

content.text:
Fix five, skip the rest.

**Fix**
- **`wt prune` ignores unpushed commits.** This is the only one left that can lose work. Prune force-deletes the branch, and a closed PR says nothing about commits you made after it closed. Treat unpushed like dirty: skip and report.
- **Hooks skipped by prune and the dashboard close.** If you have `pre_close = ["docker compose down"]`, two of the three ways to close a worktree leave the stack running. The fix is to route all three through one close function, which also removes duplicated code.
- **`wt init` exits 0 on failure.** `wt new -i --run "claude ..."` starts an agent in a worktree whose install failed. A one-line change, and it matches what you already did for rebase conflicts.
- **Auto-install from a subdirectory.** Same bug class as the close and rename fixes, and the same one-line cure: take the root from git instead of the current directory.
- **`wt open` on merged or closed PRs.** Replace the lookup with `gh pr view <branch> --web`. That deletes code, removes the dead warning, and makes the command work after merge.

**Skip**
- **Unpushed hole with no upstream.** It needs a non-default git setting to trigger. The fix adds a second definition of "unpushed" that would misfire on squash-merged branches. Not worth it.
- **`wt rename` via the rename API.** Better behaviour, but it is a rewrite of the remote half of the command for something you run rarely. Do it only if losing review threads has actually bitten you.
- **`wt list` speed.** Parallel git calls add concurrency to code that is fast enough at ten worktrees. Fix the help text instead, if anything.
- **Dashboard `R` fetching per worktree.** Wasteful but harmless, and the failures are already ignored.
- **`wt -C dir prompt` update check.** Nobody puts `-C` in a prompt command.
- **Update cache location.** Moving it means a migration for zero user benefit.
- **`wt new --from #123` accepting closed PRs.** I'd call this a feature. Checking out a closed PR is a reasonable thing to want, and `--from` is the explicit route.

**Yours to do:** `make clean` for the stale builds.

content.text:
All five are in. Tests, vet and lint pass, and I ran each one end to end in a scratch repo except `wt open`. Nothing is committed.

- **`wt prune` keeps unpushed work.** A stale worktree with unpushed commits is now skipped and reported, the same as one with uncommitted changes.
- **One close path.** `wt close`, `wt prune` and the dashboard close now share a single function, so `pre_close` and `post_close` hooks run for all three. In the dashboard the hooks run silently, since it owns the screen. There is a new test for it in `internal/cmd/close_test.go`.
- **`wt init` exits 1 when a step fails.** `wt new -i --run "..."` no longer starts the command after a failed init.
- **Auto-install after rebase works from a subdirectory.** It looks for the lockfile at the worktree root.
- **`wt open` opens merged and closed PRs.** It hands the branch to `gh pr view --web`, and the dead warning is gone.

README, `CLAUDE.md` and the config comments now say that the close hooks run for prune and the dashboard too.

Three behaviour changes to know about:
- When init fails under `wt new -i`, wt also skips `post_new` hooks and prints no JSON. The worktree itself still exists.
- A failing `pre_close` hook now blocks a prune or dashboard close of that worktree, as it already did for `wt close`.
- `wt close` prints "Closing worktree" before the `pre_close` hooks run rather than after.

Not verified: `wt open` and the dashboard close in a live session. Both need an authenticated `gh` or a real terminal, so they are covered by compile and the shared-close test only.

content.content:
# Rex

Manage sessions, arrange panes, and run commands with the Rex command-line tool.

## Overview

Run the installed `rex` command directly. It locates and connects to the Rex
server automatically. Use the CLI's built-in commands to manage Rex without
scripting the app's interface or communicating with the server's socket directly.

## Identify your session and pane

Rex sets two environment variables when it opens a terminal. The context provided
at the start of your session includes their values:

- `REX_SESSION` identifies your session. Pass `-s "$REX_SESSION"` to select it
  for a command.
- `REX_BLOCK` identifies your terminal pane. Pass `-b "$REX_BLOCK"` to select
  that pane, for example when creating a split beside it.

These values identify where you're running. The user may be viewing a different
session or pane. Choose the target based on the request:

- **"Here", "beside you", or no location at all.** Use `$REX_SESSION` and

Send key presses to a terminal

Each KEY uses Rex's key binding syntax. Join modifiers with +, as in ctrl+c or
shift+left. A bracketed name such as [Slash] selects a physical key. By default,
Rex sends a press followed by a release for each key. Use --action to send one
action instead.

not receive physical keyboard input. The generated text and physical key may
differ on other layouts. Use rex send when exact text matters.

  rex send-key shift+left shift+left

content.text:
Everything I flagged as unverified now checks out except the parts that need your real GitHub account.

**Verified with a stand-in `gh` returning canned PR data** (old binary against new):
- Bare `wt` now prints `PR #7  1 approved, CI passing`. The old binary printed nothing.
- `wt prune --dry-run` leaves a branch with an open PR alone. The old binary listed it as stale because of its earlier merged PR.
- `wt open` calls `gh pr view <branch> --web` and exits 0. The old binary failed with "no PR found" for a merged PR.

**Verified in a live dashboard, driven through a Rex tab:**
- `c` on a clean worktree and `c` then `y` on a dirty one both removed the worktree and branch. `pre_close` and `post_close` ran for each.
- The hooks echoed to stdout and stderr on purpose, and the screen stayed clean.
- `r` on the main row reports "up to date".
- Diff stats: the old binary showed `+1 −50 across 2 files` for a one-line branch that was one commit behind. The new one shows `+1 −0 across 1 file`.
- A file under `my dir/` shows its full path. The old binary showed `file.txt`.
- A long commit subject now fills the line before the ellipsis.

**For you to check**, since these need real GitHub and a browser. From a repo with an authenticated `gh` and a few worktrees:

```fish
cd ~/Dev/wt; and make build; and set -l wt ~/Dev/wt/wt

# 1. In a worktree whose PR is open: expect a "PR #N  ..." line with reviews and CI
$wt

# 2. In a worktree whose PR is merged or closed: expect the browser to open it
$wt open

# 3. Expect only merged/closed worktrees, none with an open PR or unpushed commits
$wt prune --dry-run

# 4. A branch with an open PR that is NOT checked out: expect the watch table
$wt watch some/branch-name
```

Step 4 is the one I could not exercise at all: the watch fallback for a branch with no worktree compiles and nothing more. I also tested on macOS only, so the Linux clone path is untouched by this pass.

content.text:
# /wt-release - Release a new wt version

Tag and release a new version of wt. GoReleaser builds binaries and updates the Homebrew formula automatically.

## Steps

1. Run `git status` in the wt project root (`~/Dev/wt`) — abort if there are uncommitted changes or if `main` differs from `origin/main`
2. Run `git log --oneline -5` to show recent commits
3. Check the latest git tag with `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` to determine the current version
4. Ask the user what the new version should be (suggest a patch bump, e.g. v1.22.1 → v1.22.2)
5. Check that CI passed on HEAD: `gh run list --branch main --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD) --limit 1` — wait with `gh run watch <id> --exit-status` if it's still running, and abort if it failed
6. Run `git tag <version> && git push origin <version>`
7. Watch the release run (`gh run list --workflow release.yml --limit 1`, then `gh run watch <id> --exit-status`) and report the result
8. Update the local install: `git -C $(brew --repository mvwi/homebrew-tap) pull origin main && brew reinstall wt`, then confirm with `wt --version`

  internal/cmd/switch.go internal/cmd/switch_test.go
